purpose: Per CEO R281 P3: 'Once V2 survives the complete attack: 4-segment fluidic circuit → controlled occlusion valves → pressure sensors → flow sensors → programmable disturbance generator → controller → data acquisition → blinded test protocol. The buyer should be able to reproduce the comparison without trusting our simulator.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXVI — no self-certification. Physical bench allows independent validation. Article XXXV — closed-loop epistemic control: bench is the 'experiment' slot of the loop.
design_principle: The buyer builds this bench, runs our frozen protocol, and reproduces (or refutes) our simulator findings on physical hardware. They do NOT need to trust our software.

bench_architecture.overview: 4-segment parallel hydraulic circuit mimicking multi-segment CSF shunt. Programmable occlusion, pulsatile flow, sensor noise injection, controller running V2 algorithm.
bench_architecture.schematic_text: [CSF Reservoir 37°C] → [Pulsatile Pump] → [Proximal Pressure Sensor] → [4-way Manifold] → 4× [Segment: Flow Sensor → Variable Orifice Valve → Programmable Occlusion Resistor] → [Distal Reservoir]
bench_architecture.control_loop: Sensors → DAQ → Controller PC (Python, runs V2) → Valve Drivers → Valves
bench_architecture.form_factor: Bench-top, ~60cm × 40cm × 30cm. Acrylic frame. No cleanroom needed.

programmable_disturbance_generator.purpose: Reproduce all 9 attack modes from the simulator on physical hardware

attack_modes.name: none
attack_modes.method: Run with default parameters, no disturbances

attack_modes.name: noise_3x
attack_modes.method: Software adds 3x Gaussian noise to sensor readings before controller

attack_modes.name: sensor_dropout
attack_modes.method: Software randomly sets sensor readings to 0 for 60s every 5-15 min

attack_modes.name: fast_occlusion
attack_modes.method: Programmable resistor closes 5x faster than default (full closure in ~12 min vs 60 min)

attack_modes.name: slow_occlusion
attack_modes.method: Programmable resistor closes 5x slower (full closure in ~5 hours)

attack_modes.name: wrong_model
attack_modes.method: Controller assumes exponential decay; actual resistor closure is linear

attack_modes.name: actuator_saturation
attack_modes.method: Software caps valve command at 70% (simulates degraded actuator)

attack_modes.name: controller_delay
attack_modes.method: Software adds 5-second delay between controller output and valve command

programmable_disturbance_generator.implementation: All attack modes are SOFTWARE-INJECTED via the DAQ/controller. No hardware reconfiguration needed between attacks. This makes the bench reproducible and fast to test.

blinded_test_protocol.purpose: Prevent confirmation bias. Lab analyst does not know which controller is running.
procedure: 1. Controller PC runs one of 4 arms (A/B/C/D) selected by a randomization script
2. The arm identity is encrypted and stored in a file the analyst cannot read
3. Analyst runs the frozen protocol (9 attacks × 5 seeds = 45 runs per arm)
4. Analyst records all sensor data and metrics
5. After all 180 runs (4 arms × 45), the encryption key is revealed
6. Results are unblinded and compared to simulator predictions
7. Any discrepancy between bench and simulator is documented
blinded_test_protocol.blinding_integrity: The randomization script uses a cryptographic hash. The analyst cannot influence which arm runs. The encryption key is held by a third party (e.g., lab director not involved in testing).

data_acquisition_specification.format: CSV per run, 10 columns, 86400 rows (24h × 3600 s/h × 10 samples/s)
data_acquisition_specification.storage: ~50 MB per run, ~9 GB for full 180-run validation

acceptance_criteria_bench.purpose: Pre-registered criteria for bench validation. Cannot be silently relaxed (Article XXVII).

criteria.metric: V2 vs B time-to-failure ratio under noise_3x
Bench results match simulator within tolerance
criteria.threshold: All metrics within ±30% of simulator prediction

acceptance_criteria_bench.honest_note: If bench results differ from simulator by >30%, the simulator is WRONG. This is not a failure of the bench — it is a falsification of the model. The simulator must be revised before any buyer claims.

what_buyer_receives: Frozen V2 simulator code (10_V2_comparison.py, SHA-256 hash)
Full bill of materials with vendor links
what_buyer_does: 2. Assemble bench (4-8 weeks, no special skills needed beyond basic lab setup)
3. Run 180 simulations (4 arms × 9 attacks × 5 seeds = 180 runs, 24h each = 180 days at 24/7, or ~6 months at 1 run/day)
4. Submit results in specified JSON format
5. Unblind and compare to simulator predictions
6. Publish results (confirm or refute) alongside our pre-registered predictions
estimated_timeline: 3-6 months from component procurement to results
estimated_cost: $7-8K materials + $0-50K personnel (depending on whether buyer uses internal staff or hires)
